summary: Reproduced the OpenAI SDK coercion that serialized Responses streaming snapshot created_at values as floats, then normalized response-bearing events at the shared final SSE serialization seam used by both Harmony and non-Harmony streams. Added regression coverage for created, in-progress, completed, and failed snapshots plus an independent non-response delta passthrough boundary.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the patch, OpenAI SDK 2.6.1 serialized created_at as JSON float 1786588600.0 for response.created, response.in_progress, and response.completed. Raw output is retained in reports/j-a6adad9aad7b/raw/reproduction-before.txt.

After the patch, the production serializer emitted JSON integer 1786588600 for response.created, response.in_progress, and response.completed. Raw output is retained in reports/j-a6adad9aad7b/raw/reproduction-after.txt.

All 10 focused streaming tests passed. The generator fixture asserted integer created_at values on created, in-progress, and completed SSE snapshots; the independent serializer boundary asserted failed snapshots are integers and non-response delta serialization is unchanged.
Changed Python files compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect was reproduced and validated entirely at the OpenAI SDK/Pydantic final JSON serialization boundary; no model execution or GPU behavior participates in this wire-type coercion.

remaining_limitations: No live HTTP model-server run was performed because model weights were not needed for this deterministic serialization defect; transport and model execution were therefore not requalified.
The actual non-Harmony stream generator fixture was exercised. The Harmony path uses the same new serializer call but was not run through a full Harmony model fixture.
The prepared environment did not include black or ruff; py_compile, git diff --check, and the focused unit suite passed.
